newsitem.title: USA: SEVERAL U.S. CITIES KEEN ON 2008 OLYMPICS.
newsitem.headline: SEVERAL U.S. CITIES KEEN ON 2008 OLYMPICS.

text.p: Six U.S. cities are keen to host the 2008 Summer Olympics, but the U.S. Olympic Committee has not yet decided whether to propose an American city, a spokesman said on Friday.
"The Executive Committe of the USOC will hold a meeting next week (January 18) to decide when is the next time we want to put forth a U.S. city," USOC spokesman Mike Moran said.
Boston, Chicago, Cincinnati, Houston, New York and Seattle have expressed interest in the games.
The International Olympics Committee picks the site and Moran said the USOC needed to gauge the interest in another U.S. city.
Atlanta hosted the 1996 games and the United States hosted the Summer Games in Los Angeles in 1984 and the Winter Games in Lake Placid, New York, in 1980.
